description: Field-scoped, append-only workstream event — one per-entry file per (workstream, field) mutation, in the review-trail-style collision-safe idiom (write-new, keyed by date+workstream+session-id, never mutated in place). The generator (C3) folds all events for a given (workstream, field) pair by (sequence, session-id) — NEVER wall-clock — to compute that field's current value at render time. Two sessions completing DIFFERENT deliverables of the SAME workstream both survive because each event names its own field; two sessions racing the SAME (workstream, field) both persist as distinct files (file-survival) and the fold picks one deterministic winner (fold-correctness). Spec backlink: DoE-claude:pln-project-tracker-render-from-qu-41e413 § Approach (fold rule, fold granularity) / § Substrate (field-scoped events) / § Chunks C2.

workstream.description: The workstream_id this event mutates a field of. FK to state/workstreams/<workstream_id>.yaml.

field.description: The field-scoped sub-state this event mutates — e.g. 'status', 'deliverable[0].done', 'order'. The generator folds strictly per-(workstream, field) pair; two events naming different fields on the same workstream both survive the fold independently (§ Approach finding 2).

value.description: The new value for the named field, as of this event.

sequence.description: Explicit machine-independent order key — obtained by the writer counting existing events for this (workstream, field) and adding 1 at append time. The fold picks the highest-sequence event, NEVER the most-recent-by-wall-clock (clock skew, NTP correction, and DST make wall-clock non-monotonic across machines and can tie at file-mtime/ISO-second granularity). A lost sequence race just retries to the next integer via the same _write_out_path_excl retry-with-suffix idiom used at the file layer — no new collision primitive needed.

session.description: Session id of the writer. Lexical tiebreaker when two events for the same (workstream, field) carry the same sequence — deterministic, not causal, and independent of directory read order or which write physically lands on disk first.

coordinator_root_path.description: Dual-tenant discriminator — the git root path of the repo this event's workstream belongs to. Mirrors workstream.schema.json's coordinator_root_path (same composite-natural-key component claude-klabauter's trackers.py already uses); required so the generator can filter a dual-tenant state/workstreams/events/ directory (the claude-klabauter-hosted meta-repo case) to only the current repo's entries.

supersedes.description: Optional retraction/correction pointer — lets a session directly retract or correct a prior event (by referencing its filename or an equivalent stable handle) without the fold needing to infer causality from timestamps.
